title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'Reunion', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the last hourglass, on the shelf: a tall glass hourglass about 40 cm, dark wood ends, sand running from the upper bulb into a cone in the lower, flames standing along the upper rim and smoke leaving upward; it never runs out and its fire only grows (full, unlit, running, small flame, running, full fire, the one still alight, ember lifting off the rim); the hand hourglass (x12): hand-sized hourglass, 18 cm, dark wood ends, the glass smouldering with a small flame at the neck; as it burns out it slumps and its outline goes out run by run (lit, sand running, guttering, outline broken, out, slumped, smoke only); the old snapshot: a faded square snapshot with a white border: the brothers decades younger, mid-run, one holding a football (held up, insert: the old pose, matched by the living restaging); the worn football: worn brown leather American football, white laces (held, tossed (2-frame spin)); the wall screen: large flat black-framed screen on the white wall showing a football game in green and white (game on, goal flash); the phone: black smartphone held up landscape (raised, flash); the white niche shelf: an arched lit niche in the white temple wall with a floating shelf (lit); the porch light: a single bare bulb in a small tin shade over the temple's side porch, wooden steps below, a few string bulbs looping along the eave (off, switching on, on, reflected in the pool). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
